narrative:
The model determined that you have a 59% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the level of savings you have, and the purpose of the loan. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single biggest reason for the rejection. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have a negative balance, while 59% have no checking account at all. This status pushed the prediction strongly toward bad credit risk.

Your lack of savings (unknown or none) was the second most important factor, but it actually worked in your favor. Most approved applicants also have very little or no savings, so this commonality slightly reduced the risk score.

The fact that you are requesting the loan to buy a new car was the third most influential element. While new-car loans are fairly common, this purpose still increased the predicted risk compared with other loan reasons such as home-related purchases that lenders see more favorably.

Taken together, the negative checking-account status and the new-car purpose outweighed the positive effect of your savings profile, leading to the denial.

You should focus on building a positive checking-account balance for at least several months, consider saving even a modest amount, and explore whether a different loan purpose or a smaller amount might improve your chances. Reapply once these areas show clearer stability. (248 words)
